entities.summary:
Gaius Centenius was a Roman propraetor during the Second Punic War (218-201 BCE) who played a significant role in the Battle of Lake Trasimene (217 BCE), a pivotal event in the war against Hannibal.

As a key figure in the Roman army, Centenius was part of a larger strategy to counter Hannibal's invasion of Italy. The battle, which occurred on August 21, 217 BCE, was a decisive Roman victory that thwarted Hannibal's attempt to conquer Italy and ultimately contributed to the Roman victory in the war.

The defeat of Hannibal at the Battle of Lake Trasimene had far-reaching consequences for the Roman Republic, as it marked a turning point in the war and paved the way for Roman victory. Centenius' role in the battle and his leadership of the Roman army played a crucial part in this outcome.

Centenius' legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he represents an important chapter in the history of the Roman Republic and its expansion into Italy.
